acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Raptors family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Roc, T5, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Airspace Sovereign archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two wind construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Vast natural raptor with mountain-eagle anatomy, weathered layered plumage, one damaged outer primary, and an unmistakable full-span silhouette.
Signature mechanic: Three Flight Bands: successive feather rows lift to assign a lower Raptor to one altitude band before the Roc seals the remaining band with its own dive.
battlefieldDuty: Create alternating high, crosswind, and ground-skimming flight bands before a full-span arena dive.
constructionDimensions: Outer feathers partially dissipate into directional pressure filaments while the bird's body, head, and load-bearing wing bones remain opaque.
Compression arcs, dust spirals, and feather-edge wakes make flight bands and dive lines explicit.
counterplay: Clear the assigned bird to create a safe vertical pocket before the Roc commits to the other bands. Affinity signal: The pressure envelope collapses to a still shoulder, talon, or landing perch during the authored punish window.
forbiddenTreatments: Omnidirectional clouds that obscure the attack shadow
identityInvariants: Every form retains an avian body with two wings, two taloned legs, hooked beak, feathered tail, and species-appropriate head rather than humanoid arms or torso.
Tier escalation uses wingspan, feather structure, facial disc, talon mass, scars, and flight behavior rather than worn equipment.
Shadow shape, tail fan, primary-feather angle, talon extension, perch choice, and landing route keep aerial attacks readable.
telegraph: One feather row rises and its assigned bird calls once while the matching air lane gathers debris.
